label: BANSAL S07: opioid with carbamazepine, phenytoin or phenobarbital
title: Opioid with carbamazepine, phenytoin or phenobarbital in epilepsy
statement: Co-prescription of opioid analgesics with carbamazepine, phenytoin, or phenobarbital to a patient with epilepsy [67–71]

source.document: Bansal N, et al. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care. BMC Med 2024;22:5, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x

plain_summary: In a person with epilepsy, these antiseizure medicines can make some opioids less effective by increasing their breakdown.

needs_facts.meets: Epilepsy was present when both medicines were prescribed together. An unknown answer leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Epilepsy present when both medicines were prescribed together
Epilepsy absent when both medicines were prescribed together

needs_facts.what: Reason for the methadone course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only when the product and record leave its use unclear and the other evidence fits. Count this course for chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care. Exclude opioid dependence and other uses. Unknown use leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care
Another use, including cancer pain or palliative care

needs_facts.what: Timing of the opioid and antiseizure medicine prescriptions under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if the supplies are within 60 days and the dates and directions leave prescribed overlap unclear. Overlapping prescriptions qualify and separate courses do not. An unknown answer leaves this pair possible.

options.words: Prescribed for use at the same time

medicine_groups.name: Opioid analgesics
medicine_groups.note: Count opioid analgesics used for pain, including generic packs labelled with the ingredient and company name. Exclude cough linctuses and buprenorphine products used for opioid dependence, including depot injections. Count Temgesic sublingual tablets for pain. Exclude Biodone Forte, Opod-P Liquid and Physeptone Liquid. Count Physeptone tablets supplied for pain. If the form or reason for methadone use is unclear, report at most a possible finding and ask whether it was supplied for pain.

medicine_groups.name: Enzyme-inducing antiseizure medicines
medicine_groups.note: Phenobarbital is also written phenobarbitone. No brand is listed because it is supplied by ingredient name.

rule_for_models: For a person over 18 with chronic non-cancer pain and epilepsy during treatment, cite the epilepsy line and a Group A opioid and Group B antiseizure medicine whose prescribed courses overlap. Exclude separate courses and epilepsy ruled out. When overlap is unclear and supplies are within 60 days, or an otherwise qualifying pair has uncertain age, epilepsy status or methadone use for pain, report only a possible finding and ask only about the missing detail. Use a methadone answer for that course and a timing answer for that pair of prescriptions.
cannot_be_seen: Why the antiseizure medicine is taken if no condition is recorded, how well the pain and the seizures are controlled, and whether the opioid dose has been adjusted.
ask_the_gp: A review of the pain treatment for this person, with the effect of the antiseizure medicine on the opioid in mind, and confirmation that the person has epilepsy.
